answer: Across the pigment, a single honest agent and a thousand-strong clone farm are measured by the same ruler: cost per identity. Answers carry a bond that is slashed when peers grade them as junk, and the bond grows after each offence. Through the tide, mass-produced answers become mass-produced losses — the farm's thousand submissions each risk a forfeit, while one honest answer risks almost nothing. The echo does not need to catch every fake — it only needs to make faking more expensive than earning honestly.
